key_insight: El Agente Estructural is a multimodal, natural-language-driven agent that generates and edits molecular geometries in 3D by combining vision-language models with domain-informed tools, allowing expert-like, precise control over atoms and functional groups.
problem_solved: Provides a controllable, interpretable alternative to black-box generative models by enabling precise, human-style 3D manipulation of molecular structures for autonomous chemistry and molecular modelling workflows.
method: Multimodal pipeline that integrates vision-language models with a comprehensive set of chemistry-aware tools to generate and manipulate 3D geometries.
Natural-language commands mapped to expert-inspired action primitives (e.g., atomic/functional-group replacement, localized edits) to replicate human manipulation workflows.
Domain-informed validation and tooling to ensure chemically plausible edits and to enable seamless integration into autonomous modelling and simulation loops.
impact: Delivers fine-grained, interpretable control for molecular design tasks, lowering the barrier for domain experts to specify edits in natural language and enabling faster, more reproducible AI-driven chemistry workflows.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: vision-language model + chemistry toolset -> 3D geometry editor illustrating data flow and action primitives.
Before/after molecular renderings highlighting precise atomic or functional-group edits (with annotated natural-language commands).
UI mockup: user issues a text command and the agent shows stepwise manipulations and validation checks.
Conceptual comparison chart: control granularity and interpretability of Estructural versus black-box generative models.
paper_title: El Agente Estructural: An Artificially Intelligent Molecular Editor
paper_authors: Changhyeok Choi, Yunheng Zou, Marcel Müller, Han Hao, Yeonghun Kang
